title: SYSK Selects: How Bigfoot Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2013 episode "How Bigfoot Works," chosen by Josh. The hosts examine both sides of the Bigfoot question. They discuss Dr. Melba Ketchum's claimed nuclear DNA paper, the North Georgia Bigfoot hoax, Native American sasquatch legends and the name's origin, typical reported traits (height, gait, reddish fur, smell, vocalizations), Gigantopithecus and orangutans as a possible link, the absence of bones, the Patterson-Gimlin film and the suit-maker controversy, and the hosts' skeptical and believer views. The episode ends with a listener email about a meth-contaminated house and sign-off.
topics: Mystery Science Theater 3000 Legend of Boggy Creek

segments.title: Opening and Josh's Selects introduction
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode as a SYSK Selects pick and says it explores both sides of whether Bigfoot might exist. The hosts banter about Jack Links commercials and the Messing with Sasquatch ads.

segments.title: Melba Ketchum's Bigfoot DNA paper
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a self-described veterinarian, Dr. Melba Ketchum, who claimed nuclear DNA from Bigfoot hair samples in a paper submitted for peer review. They note the sample's source was not disclosed and that her claims have drawn criticism.

segments.title: North Georgia Bigfoot hoax
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a North Georgia sheriff or deputy who displayed a supposed Bigfoot body in a freezer. It turned out to be a hoax, apparently meant to drum up business for Bigfoot tours, and the hosts debate whether that counts as fraud.

segments.title: Native American legends and the name sasquatch
segments.summary: The hosts describe Bigfoot-like legends across many Native American tribes in widely separated regions. They explain that J. W. Burns, a white schoolteacher, coined the term sasquatch in the 1920s from a word in a British Columbia-area language. Yeti legends are mentioned as well.

segments.title: Typical sasquatch traits
segments.summary: The hosts list reported characteristics: height from seven to fifteen feet, bipedal upright loping gait, long reddish-brown fur, gurgling and howling sounds, a man-like face, strong smell or no smell, wariness with curiosity, and a generally non-threatening demeanor. They mention that Bigfoot is usually alone. The Troll Hunter film is discussed briefly.

segments.title: Gigantopithecus and orangutan link
segments.summary: The hosts propose Gigantopithecus, an extinct large ape that lived in Asia, as a possible model for Bigfoot. They note its resemblance to orangutans in reddish hair, long arms, height, and solitary habits, and explain how such a creature could evade humans and leave no bones.

segments.title: Absence of bones and the coelacanth argument
segments.summary: The hosts argue that the lack of bones does not prove Bigfoot is absent. They cite bone decay, low population density, and few bone hunting expeditions. They also mention the coelacanth as an example of a supposedly extinct animal that was found alive, and note that undiscovered creatures are mostly found in the sea.

segments.title: Hoaxes, misidentification, and fake footprints
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how hoaxes and mistaken identity, such as a bear misidentified in a nighttime photo, could explain sightings. They describe fake plaster footprints with inconsistent features as easy hoaxes.

segments.title: Patterson-Gimlin film and ape suit debate
segments.summary: The hosts describe the 1967 Patterson-Gimlin film from Bluff Creek, California, and features cited as evidence, including the shoulder turn, bent knees, and rippling fur. They cover claims that a suit maker, possibly John Chambers, made the costume, and say the film has been tested for tampering with no tampering found.

segments.title: Bigfoot researchers and closing thoughts
segments.summary: The hosts mention Kathy Moskowitz Strain, a forest archaeologist searching for Bigfoot, and discuss why people want to believe, such as a lost sense of adventure. They also mention Mystery Science Theater 3000's Legend of Boggy Creek episode and Finding Bigfoot.

segments.title: Listener mail: meth house twins
segments.summary: Listener Jimmy Griffith tells a story about identical twins at Appalachian State. One twin had hallucinations and tested positive for meth, but the twins' bathtub-versus-shower habits led to a house whose bathtub had meth residue from a previous tenant. The twin's symptoms stopped after they moved out.

segments.title: Outro and contact information
segments.summary: The hosts invite skeptics and believers to write in via Twitter, Facebook, or email, and sign off.
